title: SR-1.13 Performance numbers anyone can reproduce
request: Closes G13: Docs and site claim 1.1 ms recall and 160 MB heap with no hardware; measured 4.55 ms and 183 MB. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: none.

tasks.title: Stamped bench results
requirements: the growth bench writes bench/results/<date>-<cpu>.json with CPU model, cores, RAM, Node version and every figure

the bench takes a results-directory override (a flag or an environment variable, default bench/results) and writes exactly one file there per run, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug of the CPU model>.json, holding every key it prints with the same value; a run whose own checks fail writes none
each results file records its token target, and every committed results file reproduces: a rerun at that target gives the same tokens_simulated, sessions and turns
each results file records the bench's exec_argv and the real heap limit from v8.getHeapStatistics(); heap_bound_mb is that limit or absent

criteria.statement: A results file without hardware fields fails the test

The test 'SR-1.13 bench writes results' runs node --max-old-space-size=256 scripts/growth-bench.mjs --tokens 2000000 with a results-directory override (a flag or environment variable, defaulting to bench/results) pointed at a temporary folder. It asserts four things. Exactly one file appears, named YYYY-MM-DD-<slug of os.cpus()[0].model>.json. Its cpu, cores, ram and node fields equal os.cpus()[0].model, os.cpus().length, os.totalmem() and process.version. Every key printed in the stdout JSON is in the file with the same value. Nothing is written under the repository's bench/results. The test is red at base because the base bench writes no such file.

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^SR-1.13 bench writes results$' test/bench-results.test.mjs 2>&1) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^ *ok [0-9]+ - SR-1\.13 bench writes results$' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v pat='^SR-1.13 bench writes results$' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }'

criteria.statement: Every results file records its token target (for example tokens_target). The test 'SR-1.13 committed results match the bench' reruns scripts/growth-bench.mjs with that target into a temporary folder for each committed bench/results/*.json. It asserts that tokens_simulated, sessions and turns equal the committed values. It also fails when bench/results holds no file.

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-timeout=280000 --test-name-pattern='^SR-1.13 committed results match the bench$' test/bench-results.test.mjs 2>&1) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^ *ok [0-9]+ - SR-1\.13 committed results match the bench$' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v pat='^SR-1.13 committed results match the bench$' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }'

criteria.statement: The test 'SR-1.13 heap limit recorded' runs the bench twice with --tokens 1000000: once with --max-old-space-size=256 and once with no flag. Each results file must hold exec_argv (equal to the child's process.execArgv) and heap_size_limit_mb, taken from v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit inside the bench. The limit must be at most 320 for the flagged run and above 320 for the run without the flag, and heap_bound_mb must equal heap_size_limit_mb or be absent.

tasks.title: Docs figures come from results
requirements: every latency and heap figure in docs cites a results file and names its hardware

every quantitative figure in docs and the README (a time, a size, a rate, a count of tokens or notes) cites a results file and names its hardware, not only latency and heap; a figure from simulated traffic (the growth bench's 170 million tokens) says it is simulated and gives the stored size beside it
the template site's pages under site/web/ follow the same rule while they exist (SR-6.11 retires them)
the checker reads the real docs/ and README.md (from MEMEV_DOCS_ROOT when set), and its real-docs test is never skipped
a figure counts as cited only when its paragraph links the results file, names that file's CPU model and matches the key that carries the figure's unit
the simulated-token rule covers every written form of the count (170 million, 170-million-token, 170M, 170000000) and needs the stored size (notes_mb or log_mb) beside it, not the heap

every kind of figure counts (times, sizes, rates, and counts of sessions, turns, operations and notes); a figure that no committed results file supports is removed or restated without the number, a configured limit or setting needs no results file only where its sentence states it as one, and the checker exempts no measured figure

criteria.statement: A figure in docs that is not in a results file fails

The test 'SR-1.13 cites and names' covers four fixture cases. (a) The figure is in results file R, but the paragraph has no link to bench/results/R: fails. (b) The paragraph links R but does not contain R's CPU model string: fails. (c) The paragraph links R, while the figure's value exists only in another file S, or only under a key in R whose unit differs from the figure's unit (for example 1.1 ms against log_mb 1.1): fails. (d) The paragraph links R, names R's CPU, and the figure matches the key in R with the right unit: passes.

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^SR-1.13 cites and names$' test/docs-figures.test.mjs 2>&1) && printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -Eq '^ *ok [0-9]+ - SR-1\.13 cites and names$' && printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v pat='^SR-1.13 cites and names$' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }'
